title: When a thing changes, every prose line that describes it changes in the same merge
why: shiv, Nov 1 16:30 CST, in chat to triage: "Please make it a standing thing that stale prose never makes it anymore man when things change the prose needs to be snappy to match (i think maybe we've already addressed this and we just had a past debt of this -- unclear)". Incident the same hour: a question's 'Departs from' line described main wrongly (owner, 16:23 CST).
note: What exists (read Nov 1 16:31 CST): rule speak-rewrite-superseded-in-place (CLAUDE.md) says rewrite superseded text in place; skill fresh-prose binds each claim to a checked reader; hooks/prose_judge.py model-judges only edits inside a decisions folder; lint/rule_mechanisms.json lists speak-rewrite-superseded-in-place as unmechanized. Gaps to measure first: prose outside decisions (skills, output style, README, docs/design, roadmap step text, waiting-page items, question lines) has no staleness check; nothing ties a code change to the prose that names it. Task: 1) find past debts or notes on stale prose and say whether any fix landed; 2) count stale lines on main now (a sample is fine, marked as a sample); 3) propose the one home that catches it at merge (for example a check that a PR changing a named symbol, constant, flag or path also touches or re-confirms each prose line that names it), judged by outcome and cost; picks go to triage as page questions. Done check: the mechanism is on main with a test red on a stale line and green on its fix, and the rule's entry in lint/rule_mechanisms.json names it. Needs no answer.
